name: Weekly website health checks for agency clients with Google Sheets, Slack and Gmail drafts

parameters.content:
## Weekly website health checks for agency clients with Google Sheets, Slack and Gmail drafts

**Who it's for:** web agencies, freelancers and IT teams who look after many small-business websites and want a weekly, client-ready picture of which sites need work, before the client notices.

**What it does:** every Monday (or on demand) it reads your client list from Google Sheets and checks each website twice with the Weio API: the HTTPS check looks at the bare address and `www.` the way a browser does (certificate errors, expiry, "Not secure"), and the site-facts lookup loads the home page (does it answer, mobile layout tag, title, description, a way to contact the business). Every site gets a **health score** out of 100, a severity (critical, warning or ok) and plain-English issues you can paste into a client email.

The result is written back to the client's row and appended to a **History** tab, so you can see a site's trend week by week. The workflow compares each site with last week: **new or worse critical problems** go to Slack straight away, each client with open problems gets a **Gmail draft** with their own report (drafts are never sent automatically, you review them first), and your team gets one **digest** with what got worse, what is still open, what was fixed and how many API credits are left.

Busy or rate-limited checks are not charged and are retried next run. If the API key is missing, expired or out of credit, the run stops with a clear message instead of writing half a report, and an **Error Trigger** posts to Slack if anything else fails.

**How to set up:**
1. Make a sheet with a **Sites** tab (`website`, `client`, `client_email`, `active`, plus empty `severity`, `health_score`, `issues`, `cert_expires`, `mobile_ready`, `contact_found`, `checked_at`) and a **History** tab (`checked_at`, `website`, `client`, `client_email`, `severity`, `health_score`, `change`, `issues`, `cert_expires`, `credits_left`).
2. Open **Settings**: paste the sheet URL, your team email and agency name, and adjust the day windows and limits.
3. Pick your credentials on the Google Sheets, Slack and Gmail nodes.
4. Create an n8n **Header Auth** credential named `Weio API key` (Name `Authorization`, Value `Bearer wk_...`) and select it on **Check HTTPS** and **Look up site facts**.
5. Run it once with **Execute workflow**, then activate it.

**Requirements:** Google Sheets, Slack and Gmail accounts and a Weio API key ($9 for 1,000 credits, valid 12 months, sent automatically after checkout at [weio.ai](https://weio.ai/services/site-check-api.html?utm_source=n8n&utm_medium=templates&utm_campaign=site-health)). Each website uses two credits per run (one per check); 50 sites a week is about 400 credits a month.

**Customize:** change the schedule or day windows, turn client drafts off in **Settings**, or swap Slack and Gmail for Teams or Outlook.

Made by Weio (weio.ai), a small company where AI operators do most of the work.

## 1. Start and settings
Runs every Monday at 7:00, or by hand.

In **Settings** paste your sheet URL, team email and agency name. `client_report_drafts` turns the per-client Gmail drafts on or off; the day windows set when a certificate is a warning or critical.

## 2. Read the client list
**Sites** tab: `website`, `client`, `client_email`, `active`. Rows with `active` = `no` are skipped, duplicates are removed and the run is capped at `max_sites_per_run`, because every check costs credits.

## 3. Check each site
One site at a time. **Check HTTPS** and **Look up site facts** both use your Header Auth credential **Weio API key** (`Authorization: Bearer wk_...`), one credit each. Errors come back as data, so one bad site never stops the list.

## 4. Score the site
Turns both answers into a health score out of 100, a severity and plain-English issues, and compares them with last week's row.

A missing, expired or empty API key stops the run here with a clear message.

## 5. Save results
**Update site row** writes the score and issues to the client's row (matched on `website`). **Append to history** adds one line per site per run to the History tab, so you can show a client their trend. The pause keeps you under the API rate limit.

## 6. Tell the right people
After the last site:
- **Slack** gets new or worse critical sites at once.
- Each client with open problems gets a **Gmail draft** (never sent automatically).
- Your team gets one **digest** with what got worse, what is open, what was fixed and the credits left.

## 7. Watch the watcher
If any step fails, **Error Trigger** posts to Slack, so a broken monitor never looks like a healthy list. In Workflow settings, choose this workflow as its own error workflow.
